title: Positional Rolling
shortDefinition: Positional rolling starts in a specific situation with clear win and reset conditions.
whyItMatters: It turns knowledge into timing through repetitions that open rolling rarely gives enough of.
deepExplanation: You can spar side-control escape, back retention, bodylock pass, or front-headlock defense. The key is limiting goals so feedback is clear: pass or recover, finish or escape.
beginnerView: Start in the position you need to fix instead of waiting for it in live rolling.
advancedView: Use small constraints to test one technical cue instead of winning the whole round.

ifThenExamples.if: If you lose Positional Rolling during the exchange.
ifThenExamples.then: Stop accelerating, recover the nearest body structure, then continue the technique.
ifThenExamples.why: Modern no-gi punishes forceful continuation after structure is lost.

ifThenExamples.if: If the opponent correctly answers your first line.
ifThenExamples.then: Use Positional Rolling to switch to a safer branch instead of forcing the same line.
ifThenExamples.why: A good concept turns the opponent’s reaction into information for the next decision.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Positional Rolling is a single technical trick.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: Treat it as a decision rule that appears across many positions.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Understanding the concept automatically makes it work live.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: The concept needs body signals, short cues, and positional rolling.

trainingCues: Name Positional Rolling before adding force.
Find the body signal instead of guessing generally.
If structure is lost, reset one layer first.
Drill slowly, then test with progressive resistance.
